## Shared teaching example

The workshop uses `HealthWellbeing` from
[section 4.2.4, Correlations](https://doing-meta.guide/pooling-es#correlations),
of *Doing Meta-Analysis with R: A Hands-On Guide* by Harrer, Cuijpers, Furukawa,
and Ebert (2021). The dataset contains 29 study-level summaries, with the fields
`author`, `cor`, `n`, `population`, and `country`.

Follow this dataset from source attribution and environment preparation through
metadata, versioning, analysis, reporting, and archiving. The
[workshop teaching plan](workshop_plan.qmd) gives the main learning outcome,
the programme, and delivery guidance. This page is an unpublished planning
document.

## Structure within a page

Hands-on pages state learning objectives, give each step a time allocation,
show a worked example with expected output, and end with a checkpoint and
further reading. Solutions are in collapsed callouts. Demonstration and
conceptual pages use the same structure, with the instructor running the code.
Participants follow along in their own session unless the page asks them to
watch.

Complete installations, downloads, and image builds before the session.
Keep the closing discussion even if earlier segments overrun.

## Exercise files

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `pipelines/prepare_health_wellbeing.R` | Verifies the raw file, writes the two dataset versions, records their identifiers, and selects the full version. Rerunning it reuses matching versions. |
| `pipelines/exercise/_targets_health_wellbeing.R` | Partially completed pipeline. TODO 1 connects `fit` to `studies`; TODO 2 writes the summary file. |
| `pipelines/exercise/health_wellbeing_report.qmd` | Partially completed report. TODOs add the confidence interval, an interpretation, and the provenance fields. |
| `pipelines/_targets_health_wellbeing.R` | Completed reference pipeline, used as the solution and restored by the recovery script. |
| `pipelines/health_wellbeing_report.qmd` | Completed reference report. |
| `pipelines/recover_workshop.R` | Selects the full dataset, backs up the working pipeline, and runs the reference REML pipeline. Participants keep their report edits. |
| `workspace/` | Participants' working copies, ignored by Git. |

The targets page copies the template to `workspace/_targets.R` only if no copy
exists. The book render uses the reference pipeline with a separate output
directory. Participants run the recovery script explicitly when needed.
The report reads the summary through `here::here()` and renders as standalone
HTML beside its source.

## Supplementary synthpop exercise

Page 10 uses the full dataset pin, in this order:

1. Retrieve the full `HealthWellbeing` version recorded by the preparation
   script.
2. Define `original` with a factor `population`, `z = atanh(cor)`, and
   `log_n = log(n)`.
3. Use `synthpop::syn()` with CART and seed 123; convert synthetic `z` and
   `log_n` back with `tanh()` and rounded `exp()`; generate synthetic study
   labels; inspect distributions with `compare()`. Label all generated records
   as synthetic, including their generated sample sizes.
4. Pool the original and synthetic tables with the workshop's random-effects
   model and compare the estimates.

The synthesis example is not a differential privacy guarantee, and neither a
distribution comparison nor a matching pooled estimate establishes one. The
archiving segment mentions synthetic data briefly; the exercise itself is
follow-up material.

## Development and validation status

The pages, templates, and reference files were rendered and run in the
published workshop image under R 4.4.1, including recovery from a
clean store. Rehearsing the full session in a fresh MyBinder launch and human
review remain preparation tasks.

Codex and Claude Code assisted with this page plan, the chapters, and the
teaching examples. Human review is pending.
